'''Larry Robert Seiple''' (born February 14, 1945) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player and coach. He played [[college football]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats football|Kentucky Wildcats]]. He played professionally as a [[Punter (gridiron football)|punter]] for the [[Miami Dolphins]] of the [[American Football League]] (AFL) from 1967 through 1969, and the NFL's Dolphins from 1970 through 1977. He was selected by the Dolphins in the seventh round of the [[1967 NFL draft]]. 

With the Dolphins, Seiple was a part of two [[Super Bowl]]-winning teams, [[Super Bowl VII]] in [[1972 NFL season|1972]], when the Dolphins posted the only undefeated regular and post-season record to date in NFL history, and in [[Super Bowl VIII]] in [[1973 NFL season|1973]].

'''Larry Jerome Whigham''' (born June 23, 1972) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] for nine seasons with the [[New England Patriots]] and [[Chicago Bears]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL).

Whigham played [[college football]] for the [[Louisiana–Monroe Warhawks football|Louisiana–Monroe Warhawks]] and was selected by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] in the fourth round (110th overall) of the [[1994 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1994 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1994/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-31 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was known for his enthusiasm on the field and excelled in [[special teams]] play. He made the [[Pro Bowl]] twice as a special teams player, once with New England and once with Chicago. 
 
In January 1997 he earned AFC Special Teams Player of the Week in the [[1996–97 NFL playoffs#AFC Championship: New England Patriots 20, Jacksonville Jaguars 6|AFC Championship Game]] against Jacksonville when he tackled Jaguar punter [[Bryan Barker]] on his own four-yard line, which resulted in a touchdown for the Patriots a few plays later.

On September 21, 1997, Whigham picked up 2 sacks against Rick Mirer and the Chicago Bears.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/199709210nwe.htm|title = Chicago Bears at New England Patriots - September 21st, 1997|website = [[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref>

While Whigham gained attention playing mostly special teams (he started only six games), he intercepted four passes during his career, three of which were against the NFL's all-time leading passer, [[Dan Marino]]. He intercepted two Marino passes versus [[Miami Dolphins|Miami]] on November 23, 1997, including one he returned 60 yards for a touchdown, and finished the game with a season-high four tackles to earn Player of the Game honors.

He is married to Kenyatta Whigham and now resides in Houston, Texas.

'''Laurent Duvernay-Tardif''' {{Post-nominals|country=CAN|CM|CQ}} ({{IPA|fr|lɔʁɑ̃ dyvɛʁne taʁdif|lang}}; born February 11, 1991) is a Canadian physician and former professional [[gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (American football)|guard]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[U Sports football|university football]] and attended [[medical school]] at [[McGill University]] in [[Montreal]] before being selected by the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] in the sixth round of the [[2014 NFL draft]] and playing six years on the team.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Morse |first=Ben |date=2023-09-21 |title='A player must flourish off the field to perform on the field': Ex-Chiefs star and medical doctor Laurent Duvernay-Tardif retires from NFL |url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/09/21/sport/laurent-duvernay-tardif-retire-chiefs-nfl-spt-intl/index.html |access-date=2023-10-02 |website=CNN |language=en}}</ref> Duvernay-Tardif is one of a small number of NFL players to graduate from medical school.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.wbur.org/onlyagame/2018/09/07/medical-school-mccoll-doctor-football |title=Before The NFL Had Dr. Duvernay-Tardif, There Was Dr. Milt McColl | Only A Game |publisher=Wbur.org |date=September 7, 2018 |access-date=February 11, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Martin |first=Shawn |date=2023-02-07 |title=6 NFL Players Who Became Doctors |url=https://www.wapitimedical.com/2023/02/07/nfl-players-who-became-doctors/ |access-date=2023-10-15 |website=Wapiti Medical Staffing |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Greaney |first=Aine |date=2024-01-13 |title=8 NFL Players-Turned-Doctors |url=https://www.boardvitals.com/blog/nfl-players-turned-doctors/ |access-date=2024-01-23 |website=BoardVitals Blog |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wallace |first=Claire |date=2023-11-02 |title=NFL players turned orthopedic surgeons |url=https://www.beckersspine.com/orthopedic/58158-nfl-players-turned-orthopedic-surgeons.html |access-date=2024-01-23 |website=www.beckersspine.com |language=en-gb}}</ref> He was made a [[National Order of Quebec#Knight|Knight]] of the [[National Order of Quebec]] in 2019 and enrolled at [[Harvard University]] to get a [[Master of Public Health]] degree the following year. In December of 2024, he was appointed as a Member to the [[Order of Canada]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 December 2024 |title=A celebration of Canadian excellence: Governor General appoints 88 individuals to the Order of Canada |url=https://www.gg.ca/en/media/news/2024/appointments-order-canada-december |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241227151637/https://www.gg.ca/en/appointments-order-canada-december-2024 |archive-date=27 December 2024 |access-date=3 January 2025 |website=Governor General of Canada}}</ref>

Duvernay-Tardif opted out of the [[2020 NFL season]] due to concerns over the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] and returned to Canada to work in a [[Nursing home|care facility]]. As a result of his efforts on and off the field in 2020, he was named a co-winner of the [[Lou Marsh Award]], given annually to Canada's top athlete, as well as the [[Sports Illustrated Sportsperson of the Year|''Sports Illustrated'' Sportsperson of the Year]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 30, 2023 |title=Every Sports Illustrated Sportsperson of the Year |url=https://www.si.com/sports-illustrated/sports-illustrated-sportsperson-year-covers |access-date=December 7, 2025 |website=SI |language=en-US}}</ref> He returned to the NFL in 2021 after being traded to the [[New York Jets]] for two seasons.

He announced his retirement from the NFL on September 21, 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.cnn.com/2023/09/21/sport/laurent-duvernay-tardif-retire-chiefs-nfl-spt-intl/index.html| title ='A player must flourish off the field to perform on the field': Ex-Chiefs star and medical doctor Laurent Duvernay-Tardif retires from NFL|first=Ben|last=Morse|publisher=CNN|date=September 21, 2023}}</ref>
